deities: Thillai Kali (Brahma Chamundeeshwari — four-faced Kali, facing west)
Kali Amman in Ugra roopam (facing east)
Dakshinamurthy in female form (rare idol, praised as Sri Kadambavana Dakshina Rupini)
festivals: Special poojas on Sundays (Rahu Kalam), Pournami (full moon) and Amavasai (new moon)

history.dynasty: Chola — built by King Kopperunchinga (one review says 'almost 900 years old')
history.summary: The Thillai Kali Amman Temple on the northern outskirts of Chidambaram (about 1.8 km from the Nataraja temple, address N Main Rd) is the Kali shrine of Thillai, distinct from the Nataraja temple. History: built by the Chola king Kopperunchinga (reported as almost 900 years old; foundation-date precision is unverified). Legend: Shiva and Shakthi held a dance contest at Thillai; when Shiva performed the Urdhva Tandava (lifting his leg to replace his falling earring) — which Shakthi, as a woman before the assembled sages, could not perform — the angered goddess left the sabha and settled at the edge (ellai) of Thillai as Thillai Kali/Ellai Kali. Brahma pacified her by praising her as Veda Nayagi and asking her to take four faces denoting the four Vedas; hence she is worshipped as Brahma Chamundeeshwari with four faces, facing west. The temple is regarded as the mandatory concluding visit of the Chidambaram pilgrimage circuit. Timings conflict across sources (morning opening 6:00 AM vs 6:30 AM) — verify locally.

name: Thillai Kali Amman Temple
town_description: Chidambaram is a temple town in Cuddalore district, east-central Tamil Nadu. The Kali temple stands on N Main Road on the northern edge of town, about 1.8 km from the Thillai Nataraja temple.

travel.airport: Chennai International Airport — about 235 km; Pondicherry — about 65 km (verify).
travel.road: On N Main Road at the northern edge of Chidambaram town; auto/taxi from the Nataraja temple and Chidambaram station.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Vaikasi (May-June) for the 13-day Visaka festival.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM to 12:00 Noon; 4:30 PM to 8:30 PM (verify locally; some sources say 6:30 AM opening). Heavy crowds on Rahu Kalam and weekends. Entry free.
